Airports used to let you buy a ticket in cash and walk straight to the gate. Now you can't even grab an Advil off a shelf without someone unlocking a case and walking you to the register like a suspect.

Kevin's point isn't that none of that is real. It's that none of it is supposed to be the thing that decides how you feel. The outside world can get stranger, more locked-down, more chaotic every year - that's its nature. Your internal state was never supposed to be hostage to it.

Most people never make that split. They let whatever's happening out there decide what's happening in here.
